SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Package Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Process note:** The Seller's package asks us to skip everything marked [STANDARD] because it was "reviewed and cleared by both sides." Nothing in this package has been agreed by Wattlebridge. The [STANDARD] labels are the Seller's own, and several of those clauses conflict with our playbook. All 16 issues are reviewed below. The disclosure letter is also dated as at 22 September 2026, so we should ask for a bring-down to today.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% of price, AUD 4,800,000 (Cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** 25%, AUD 6,000,000. The 20% figure is our conditional fallback and needs prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft. None has been given.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and open at 25% / AUD 6.0m. Do not concede 20% without Amelia Frost's written authority, because the fallback is not available otherwise.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000 with excess-only recovery (Cl 12.2).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000 with first-dollar recovery once exceeded.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. The Seller's figures are five times our de minimis and five times our basket, and excess-only recovery removes the first dollar.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months from Completion for general claims (Cl 12.3/13). Any limitation applies to all claims unless expressly excluded.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general claims. 18 months is a fallback that needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given. Carve-outs for fundamental, title and fraud claims must be explicit, not implied.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the 18-month period and the "applies to all claims" default. Open at 24 months with express carve-outs.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Title and capacity are not administrative items and must sit in their own regime.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply "to all Claims of any nature" (Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5). The package does not mention a fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. This cannot be waived by anyone.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. The Seller's wording would catch fraud claims, and the absence of an express carve-out is a gap that must be closed in the SPA text.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the full data room (through DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Disclosure Letter 1.1 and 1.2; Schedule 7).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific fair disclosure only. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and delete 1.1 and 1.2. General data room disclosure would make our warranties close to meaningless.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** No Buyer claim for any matter known to the Buyer or its advisers, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (Cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions deleted. Any qualifier must name Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Delete Cl 8.3. A "discoverable" standard would shift the risk of Seller warranty breaches onto us because we ran diligence.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours only. Consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent (Cl 3/6.3). Disclosure Letter 2 confirms there is no final written consent and no evidence the conditions are met.
- **Buyer wants:** Effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion, not on delivery. Reasonable endeavours is not enough for a material customer consent. Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, roughly 30% of FY26 revenue.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Make effective consent plus evidence of satisfied conditions a pre-Completion condition.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding, to be addressed by a release provided after Completion (Cl 2/7). Disclosure Letter 3 confirms the facility has not been repaid and no discharge is included.
- **Buyer wants:** A current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. A post-Completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Pay out at Completion from the funds flow. Post-Completion releases are an exception requiring the undertaking and approval.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 closing bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. Disclosure Letter 5 confirms the amounts are missing from the funds flow and on-costs are not addressed.
- **Buyer wants:** A specific funds-flow line for the bonuses, or Seller funding. Triggered on-costs (payroll tax, super) must be quantified and covered. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the silent exclusion. Require an itemised line, a quantified on-cost estimate, and Seller funding of the full amount and on-costs.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate" (Cl 11.1). The AUD 180,000 open amount is not independently verified in either direction (Disclosure Letter 4). DD-004 cl 7.3 ties transfer of SOW3 Project Materials to payment of all SOW3 fees.
- **Buyer wants:** A broadened indemnity that preserves the SOW3 cure, so that Ironquay's IP transfer is secured on payment. Verify the AUD 180,000 with bank records or Ironquay confirmation.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the narrow indemnity and broaden it. Do not treat the AUD 180,000 as proven either way until verified.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter" not expected to be material (Cl 4.6/Schedule 6).
- **Buyer wants:** Preserve logs, complete the investigation, and require regular updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. The record shows about 1,240 records and an unknown access position, so "not material" is not established.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the "not material" characterisation. Require log preservation, investigation, and updates. The deal team should also consider whether a specific indemnity is needed. That is not a playbook position and is for the team to decide.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000, described as ordinary-course costs. Disclosure Letter 8 says it is unclear whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer wants:** Assess the contracts. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** Assess before accepting the ordinary-course label. Request the contracts and terms. Do not apply an automatic price deduction or Debt treatment.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP are "settled under the general regime," and the general limitations apply to all claims (Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5).
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories kept separate, with no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Each category needs its own regime and cannot be folded into the general limits.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced by" the Company share register at DD-012 (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter 10).
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. DD-012 is a Seller-supplied internal record and is not independent proof.
- **Recommendation:** Reject DD-012 as sufficient. Require independent searches (for example ASIC company extracts, PPSR search), the executed transfer, and evidence of corporate authority.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime" (Seller update).
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP terms left OPEN. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution until the terms are negotiated.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "settled" statement. Keep the Tax and IP terms open and out of the general regime.
